newsitem.title: PERU: Peru hostage crisis is tourist draw.
newsitem.headline: Peru hostage crisis is tourist draw.

text.p: Inca ruins, Indian handicrafts and...er, hostages.
The standoff at the Japanese embassy residence in Lima, where Marxist rebels were holding 104 VIPs hostage for an eighth day on Wednesday, has turned into Peru's latest tourist draw.
"This doesn't happen every day," gushed Canadian visitor Scott Ewert as he gawked at the hordes of newsmen and police gathered near the residence.
Like Ewert, American Doug McDonald said he had changed his itinerary in Peru to squeeze in a visit to the residence.

After visiting the Inca ruins of Macchu Picchu and the Nazca lines in southern Peru, McDonald said he couldn't miss the Japanese embassy residence, which is located in the smart Lima suburb of San Isidro.
Photographers and television crews from the world's media got a taste of their own medicine as the tourists turned cameras on them to snap shots and ask questions.
